content: Clotrimazole is an antifungal medication commonly used to treat vaginal yeast infections. It alleviates symptoms such as vaginal burning, itching, and discharge caused by the infection. This medication belongs to the azole antifungal class and works by inhibiting the growth of the yeast responsible for the infection. It is available in two forms: a vaginal cream and a vaginal tablet. Before using clotrimazole for self-treatment, consult your doctor, especially if this is your first vaginal infection. This medication is specifically effective for vaginal fungal infections and should not be used if you experience symptoms such as fever, chills, flu-like symptoms, abdominal pain, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge, as these may indicate a different condition. To use the medication, follow the instructions provided on the product packaging or by your doctor. Wash your hands before and after application. Avoid contact with your eyes, and if accidental contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. For the vaginal cream, use the applicator to insert the cream into the vagina while lying on your back with your knees bent. For the vaginal tablet, you can use either the applicator or your finger to insert the tablet into the vagina. If you experience itching or burning around the vulva, you may apply the skin cream to the affected area once or twice daily for up to seven days. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days or if your menstrual period begins. Avoid using tampons, douches, spermicides, or other vaginal products during treatment. If your condition does not improve after three days, persists for more than seven days, or recurs within two months, consult your doctor. Common side effects may include vaginal or urethral burning, itching, pain, or lower abdominal cramps. Serious allergic reactions are rare. If you experience severe symptoms or suspect an overdose, seek immediate medical attention. To prevent future yeast infections, keep the genital area dry, avoid tight clothing, and change out of damp or sweaty clothes promptly. Store the medication at room temperature and discard it properly when expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare provider for personalized advice and complete information about this medication.
